card.title: BLACK PRINCE
card.text: Only 2 units can occupy the frontline. Deployment: Retreat all units in it.
card.flavorText: The Black Prince was a British experimental heavy tank developed during the final stages of WWII. The tank was named after Edward, the Black Prince, son of Edward III and heir to the English throne, but it was officially known as Tank, Infantry, Black Prince (A43). It was designed as a continuation of the Churchill tank series, but equipped with a more powerful armament. The primary goal of the Black Prince was to mount a QF 17-pounder gun, which was highly effective against German armor, including the Panther and Tiger tanks. It was very similar to the Churchill tank design, including its thick armor. However, the larger 17-pounder gun called for a larger turret which made the tank much heavier and less mobile. The Black Prince also used the same engine as the Churchill, which resulted in a top speed of only 10.5 mph (17 km/h), far slower than other tanks of the time. Six prototypes were built by 1945, but the Black Prince never saw combat. By the time its development was completed, some faster, more versatile tanks such as the Centurion were emerging, which made the slow and heavily armored Black Prince obsolete. Consequently, the project was discontinued after the war.
